title: Punna and the Brahmana (Therigatha)
body: The Therigatha, part of the Sutta Pitaka, is a collection of verses composed by bhikkhunis. In one composition, Punna, a dasi or slave woman, describes going down to the river every morning, even in the cold, to fetch water for her master's household, frightened of punishment and of the angry words of high-class women. There she sees a Brahmana bathing in the icy water and asks him what he is afraid of. The Brahmana replies that he is doing good to prevent evil, because anyone who has done something bad is freed by washing in water. Punna answers that if this were so, all the frogs, turtles, water snakes and crocodiles would go to heaven. Instead, she tells him, he should not do the thing whose fear leads him to the water, and he should stop and save his skin from the cold.
